bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge code, the combinational clock-enable assignments gate the normal clock-enable conditions with ~fsm_invalid_q. When the slow FSM enters its invalid terminal state, fsm_invalid_q is asserted, so core_clk_en_d, io_clk_en_d, and usb_clk_en_d are forced low. This contradicts the invalid-state requirement, which says the core, I/O, and USB clock enable requests shall be forced on in the invalid state. As a result, the high-speed clocks are turned off exactly when the fast FSM may need them to remain available, preventing the invalid state from being properly propagated or recovered via clocked logic.
bug_info.fix_hint: Change the clock-enable assignments so that the invalid flag forces the clock enables to be asserted instead of suppressing them. Replace the ~fsm_invalid_q AND term with fsm_invalid_q being ORed into each clock-enable expression, keeping the normal active/low-power clock selection when the FSM is not invalid.
